body.text: "guravo mahāvajradharādajaḥ, daśadigavasthitāśca sarvabuddhabodhisattvāḥ mām samanvāharantu / bhadanto māṃ samanvāharatu / ahamevaṃnāmā anādisaṃsārāt prabhṛtipratyutpannaparyantaṃ rāga-dveṣa-mohavaśāt kāyavāṅmanasā daśākuśalāni kṛtavān, pañcānantaryāṇi, pañca tatsabhāgāni, prātimokṣasaṃvaravirodhaḥ, bodhisattvaśikṣāvirodhaḥ, guhyamantra-samayādi-virodhaḥ, samāsato 'bhyudaya-niḥśreyasavighnabhūtāḥ, saṃsārāpāyahetubhūtāśca ye ke 'pi āpattidoṣarāśayaḥ (santi) tān sarvān guruvajradharādīnāṃ, daśadigavasthitānāṃ sarvabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ, bhadantasya ca agrato deśayāmi, āviṣkaromi, na praticchādayāmi / āviṣkṛtena mama sparśavihāro bhavati,anāviṣkṛtena evanna bhavatī ti trirvadet /
body.translated_text: May the Gurus, beginning with <s>Mahāvajradhara</s>, and all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> abiding in the ten directions, pay attention to me. O Venerable One, pay attention to me. I, of such-and-such a name, from beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence) up to the present moment, due to the power of attachment, aversion, and delusion, have committed with body, speech, and mind the ten non-virtuous actions, the five heinous crimes (<s>pañcānantarya</s>), and five similar to them, transgressions against the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (monastic vows) vows, transgressions against the <s>Bodhisattva</s> (enlightenment-being) trainings, transgressions against the <s>Guhyamantra</s> (secret mantra) commitments, etc. — in brief, whatever heaps of faults and transgressions there are that are obstacles to prosperity and ultimate liberation, and causes for lower realms in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence) — all of them I confess, reveal, and do not conceal before the Gurus beginning with <s>Vajradhara</s>, all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> abiding in the ten directions, and the Venerable One. By revealing, I experience ease; by not revealing, it is not so — say this three times.
Then, after the inquiry regarding viewing the vows, one should say "<s>upāyaṃ</s>" (means) and "good" (<s>sādhu</s>).

body.text: prathamasaṃyojanavidhiḥ- evannāmāhaṃ anādisaṃsārāt prabhṛti kleśabāhulyāt pramādādivaśād vā doṣāpattirāśibahulaḥ, tān saṃghasya agrataḥ pratideṣṭukāmaḥ, ato 'nugṛhyatām iti / ante āpattita uddhṛto 'smītyatīva kṛtajño 'smīti dharmānurupakāryam anumodaye iti vadet /
body.translated_text: Method for the first connection: I, of such-and-such a name, from beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence), due to the abundance of afflictions or due to heedlessness, etc., am full of heaps of faults and transgressions. I desire to confess them before the <s>Saṅgha</s> (community); therefore, may I be graced. At the end, one should say: "I am delivered from transgressions, I am extremely grateful; I rejoice in the meritorious deeds in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> (teachings)."
The <s>Āpattideśanāvidhiḥ</s> (Method for Confession of Transgressions), composed by <s>Ācārya Dīpaṅkaraśrījñāna</s>, is concluded.

body.text: tenaiva bhāratīyopādhyāyena bhoṭīyalokacakṣuṣā bhikṣu-jayaśīlena ca anūdya nirṇītaḥ /
body.translated_text: It was translated and finalized by that very Indian preceptor, and by the eye of the Tibetan people, the monk <s>Jayaśīla</s>.
